body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is linear bias in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions: 33.6 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 12 models with a format search (of 281 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 23.2 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.8 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 8 of 10 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (agreement 100% → 0%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's), facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (token agreement 100% → 57%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (agreement 100% → 58%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): linear bias in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions (fp8_e2m5, 33.6 dB), layernorm bias in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 34.2 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), layernorm output in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions (fp8_e3m4, 35.3 dB), layernorm output in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 35.5 dB), layernorm bias in BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.6 dB), add output in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions (fp8_e3m4, 35.7 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB) and add output in BAAI/bge-base-en (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): div outputs end furthest from full precision, microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition keeping only -inf dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e3m4, -3.8 dB), linear in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -3.0 dB), sub in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -2.4 dB), softmax in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -1.1 dB), relu in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -1.1 dB), div in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -0.0 dB), mul in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, 0.5 dB), aten in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, 0.9 dB) and sum in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, 1.2 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e3m4 3987 (47%), fp8_e2m5 3544 (42%), fp8_e1m6 819 (9.72%), ufp8_e2m6 71 (0.84%), ufp8_e1m7 3 (0.04%), ufp8_e3m5 2 (0.02%); 0.90% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where an output's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.4 dB) and upsample in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.9 dB).

body:
2 missing capabilities keep 31 operations in 5 models (of 11 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (29 operations in 5 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 29 operations in 5 models: 29 calls (0.76% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, embedding in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions and embedding in BAAI/bge-base-en. Cost today: 0 of 29 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 2 failed and 27 wait for one; 103 workarounds proposed, 21 passing its check, 20 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An integer format for indices.** No NX8 format can hold an integer index computed from the input, so the operations reading one (add and gather) need a workaround. It affects 2 operations in 1 model: 2 calls (0.05% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: add in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions and gather in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions. title: Missing instructions: 31 operations in 5 models need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 676 of 1111 tensors passed between kernels (61%) in 11 models: 485 for attention heads split or merged, 170 for other reshapes, 18 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 446 operations (446 calls, 12% of all calls; 104 G MACs, 4.19% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 262, linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207 and linear → add (other reshapes) 70; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (208), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (88).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 676 of 1111 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 1,088 operations in 11 models (1,088 calls, 28% of all calls), most often layernorm (324), silu (210) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst -inf dB SQNR over 649 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 22, most 81 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 81 planned groups), over 11 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.4 powers of ten for bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (largest value 1.35e+05).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

10 accuracy runs produced non-finite outputs (overflow or NaN).

0 kernels use over 80% of the 1,024-word instruction memory (IMEM) bank, of 1 kernel measured.
title: Resource limits: 1,088 operations limited by the LUT and up to 81 kernel launches per pass

body:
The IPU architecture's costs across the surveyed models, ranked from most to least significant, are:

1. **Resource limits and LUT precision** are the most widespread: 1,088 operations (28% of all calls) in 11 models go through a 256-entry lookup table that caps their precision (worst −∞ dB SQNR), and 13 outputs in one model sit at the FP32 limit itself, with 6 accuracy runs producing non-finite outputs.

2. **Layout conversions** affect 675 of 1,110 tensors (61%) passed between kernels in 11 models, forcing 445 reading operations (12% of calls, 4.19% of MACs) to rearrange data — mostly for attention-head splitting/merging — though the extra cycle cost hasn't been measured yet.

3. **Quantization accuracy on NX8 formats** is measurable but moderate: model outputs keep a median 23.2 dB SQNR against full precision (worst 12.8 dB), 8 of 10 models with a prediction metric lose some accuracy, and the worst individual tensors are linear and layernorm biases at ~33–36 dB.

4. **Missing instructions** block 32 operations in 6 models — chiefly run-time addressing (29 calls, 0.76%) — but these are data-movement-only with no MACs, and none has a working workaround yet.

5. **Compute efficiency on binary formats is the least costly in absolute terms** (0% MAC utilisation over 35 cases, suggesting the pipeline can't keep multipliers fed), though this appears to be a narrow or edge-case finding rather than a broad cost across the survey.
title: Agent summary

body:
**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip)** would put 29 operations in 5 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 29 calls (0.76% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An integer format for indices** would put 2 operations in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 2 calls (0.05% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).
